stories.title: A third blind volunteer got a wireless brain implant aimed at restoring some sight
stories.summary: Surgeons at Rush University Medical Center placed the Intracortical Visual Prosthesis (ICVP), a wireless implant that bypasses the eyes and stimulates the brain's visual cortex, in a third person who is blind: 34 stimulators, 544 electrodes. It aims to restore some sight; this early study has no results on vision yet.

predictions.note: A third blind volunteer got a wireless visual-cortex implant aimed at restoring some sight: an early feasibility study with no vision results yet.

stories.title: The FDA set a 1 May 2027 decision date for uniQure's Huntington's gene therapy
stories.summary: The FDA accepted uniQure's application for AMT-130, a one-time gene therapy infused into the brain to silence the huntingtin gene, with Priority Review and a decision date of 1 May 2027. It's not approved yet: the evidence so far comes from small phase 1/2 studies, with 51 patients dosed, compared with an external control.

stories.title: OpenAI's LifeVal benchmark grades AI on everyday tasks; GPT-6 Astra averages 80.6%
stories.summary: LifeVal tests AI on everyday-life tasks drawn from time-use surveys, like finding childcare, budgeting and ordering groceries. GPT-6 Astra averaged 80.6%, up from 49.3% for GPT-5.2. It's OpenAI's way of tracking how useful AI is in daily life, and its own benchmark of its own models, not independently checked.

stories.title: A Neuralink user with ALS steers his robot vacuum around his home by thought
stories.summary: Matic Robots says Neuralink patient #22, Zach McManus, who lives with ALS, moves its robot vacuum around his home with his thoughts; he also runs his laptop, phone, TV and Xbox controller with the implant. A company claim backed by patient videos, not a published study; Neuralink's device is in clinical trials.

predictions.note: A Neuralink user with ALS runs his robot vacuum, laptop and TV by thought at home: patient videos and a company claim, not a published study.

stories.title: AI reading a wrist tracker and a blood pressure cuff flagged dangerous spikes up to 3 days early
stories.summary: In more than 4,000 adults with stage 2 high blood pressure followed for 12 months, AI analysing a portable cuff and a wrist-worn tracker flagged higher risk of a dangerous crisis up to 72 hours ahead; 97.4% of those with no alert stayed crisis-free. Preliminary research for an American Heart Association meeting, not yet peer reviewed.

stories.title: Meta reportedly built a humanoid robot prototype, Max, in three months
stories.summary: Meta built Max, a humanoid robot about 1.5 m tall and 48 kg running on NVIDIA's Jetson Thor, with China's Fourier in three months, The Information reported. Meta says it's for internal research with no plans to sell the prototypes; a second, Max 2, reportedly entered development in September.

predictions.note: Meta reportedly built a humanoid prototype in three months for internal research: another big tech step toward general-purpose robots, not yet doing real work.

stories.title: Less of one protein revved up cell recycling and cut Alzheimer's tau in fruit flies
stories.summary: Baylor researchers found that lowering the enzyme Slingshot-1 boosted autophagy, the cell's recycling system, and cut the tau clumps linked to Alzheimer's in fruit-fly models and human cells (journal Autophagy). Drugs can be designed to block enzymes like it, but this is lab work, not tested in people.

stories.title: A protein called MTR4 keeps blood vessel linings young, and boosting it let worms live longer
stories.summary: MTR4 appears to slow the ageing (senescence) of the cells lining blood vessels, an early feature of atherosclerosis, but it declines with age; boosting it extended the lives of short-lived nematode worms (Aging Cell). A possible lead for keeping blood vessels young, shown in cells and worms only, not in mice or people.

stories.title: A 24-year study of 8,200 adults linked higher BMI to faster memory decline
stories.summary: A University of Georgia study followed more than 8,200 adults over 50 for 24 years: each one-point rise in BMI went with faster decline in memory, overall thinking and executive function, most strongly in adults over 65 (Journal of Neurology). Observational: a link, not proof that extra weight causes decline.

stories.title: When Britain kept kids in school a year longer, dementia rates later fell slightly
stories.summary: In 1972 England, Scotland and Wales raised the school-leaving age from 15 to 16. A PNAS study using that change found the extra year cut the later incidence of Alzheimer's and related dementias in that generation by approximately 0.88% and softened genetic risk: a small effect, suggesting social policy can shift dementia risk.

stories.title: The nonprofit Usona has reportedly filed psilocybin for depression with the FDA
stories.summary: According to Psychedelic Alpha, the nonprofit Usona Institute has finished submitting its FDA application for psilocybin in major depressive disorder, making it the second psychedelic under FDA review; Compass Pathways expects to complete its own submission in Q4 2026. A reported filing, not an approval.

stories.title: Inflammation dampened pleasure and the urge to socialise in a small placebo-controlled study
stories.summary: In a UCLA placebo-controlled study of 40 healthy women, a low dose of endotoxin that triggers inflammation dampened pleasure and the desire to chat with another person two hours later; the dip in pleasure was back to baseline by four hours, even with inflammation still raised. A small experiment in healthy women.

stories.title: Five labs ran identical psilocybin tests in mice, and the lasting effects didn't replicate
stories.summary: Five labs at UC Berkeley, UCSF and Stanford gave mice the same psilocybin dose under identical protocols (Nature Neuroscience). The immediate effects replicated in all five, but pooled, there were no reproducible changes in anxiety- or depression-like behaviour a day later. A mouse study; the authors say it isn't evidence against human trials.

stories.title: A review of nine trials found little evidence that medical cannabis helps insomnia
stories.summary: A Cochrane review of nine studies with 537 adults found medical cannabis gave little or no clinically meaningful improvement in sleep compared with placebo, and mild side effects such as dizziness and dry mouth were more likely. The evidence is low or very low certainty and the longest study lasted 12 weeks, so the question isn't settled.

stories.title: A former paratrooper became the first person in the UK with a bionic upper arm
stories.summary: Milos Stankovic, 63, a former paratrooper from Plymouth who lost his left arm in a motorbike crash in 2025, was fitted with a lightweight bionic upper arm from Bristol's Open Bionics, a UK first. It lets the skin breathe and sweat drain, which he says cuts infection risk and discomfort.

stories.title: A wireless implant turned surplus blood sugar into waste the body flushes out, in mice
stories.summary: ETH Zurich's wireless implant uses a gold-platinum catalyst, switched on by a glucose sensor, to turn excess blood sugar into gluconate, which leaves the body in urine (Science). In diabetic mice it kept blood sugar in check and the mice lost weight, working for six weeks with no sign of tissue damage. Not yet tested in people.

stories.title: Robots raced up more than 3,000 steps on China's Mount Tai, some carrying eggs
stories.summary: About 90 teams sent robots up a 3.9 km course with more than 3,000 steps on China's Mount Tai, racing for speed or carrying fragile goods like eggs and watermelons. The fastest robot dog took 43 minutes 41 seconds, against at least two hours for most tourists. A state-media-run contest, as reported by AFP.
